justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep accepting fractions longer than 9 digits in the base regex, but add warnings and canonicalization guidance to normalize to 9 digits.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves rare high-precision R4 values, but leaves base R6 validators unable to enforce a uniform nanosecond ceiling and keeps arbitrary-precision parser burden.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: unbounded fractional seconds are hard for many parsers, databases, and generated models to handle uniformly, while a 9-digit cap aligns with common nanosecond precision. A less-breaking path exists, but it would not fully meet a base-datatype goal of bounded lexical precision. Given the rarity of sub-nanosecond dateTime values and the material validator/interoperability tradeoff of leaving them valid, the break is probably justified even though no official rationale was available in the local inputs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would retain the R4 acceptance of arbitrary-length fractional seconds and add conformance text, a best-practice warning, or profile guidance recommending rounding, truncation, or rejection above 9 digits. That would preserve all old R4 instances, but it is only a partial alternative because arbitrary-precision values would remain valid in the base R6 datatype and implementations could not rely on a hard nanosecond maximum without extra policy.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable to R4-to-R6 break avoidance: this offset change widens the lexical space and does not make R4-valid full dateTimes invalid in R6.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping mandatory offsets would improve cross-version safety, but would limit any intended support for local full date-times; that is a conformance design choice, not a less-breaking R4-to-R6 alternative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 prose still says a UTC offset SHALL be populated when hours and minutes are specified, while the R6 regex appears to accept missing offsets and even a bare trailing sign. That internal inconsistency makes the widened regex not clearly justified. However, this finding is a reverse-direction representability and runtime-conformance risk rather than an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 base-design break, so the backward-compatible alternative classification is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed for this finding because the offset widening preserves the relevant R4-valid full dateTime strings. A clearer R6 design would keep the R4 mandatory offset group for full date-times while changing the wording from time zone to UTC offset, or explicitly add local date-time support with unambiguous conformance rules. Those choices would reduce R6-to-R4 surprises, but they are not migration guidance, backport extensions, or backwards-compatible alternatives to an R4-to-R6 break.
